scope_definitions.queue_process_seconds: Outer matrix job perf_counter: Python batch process including Application, subsequent EXR/metadata validation, plus matrix postflight and frozen-file checking.
scope_definitions.application_process_wall_seconds: Inner wrapper perf_counter around subprocess.run(Application.exe), covering startup, scene/device creation, all four seeds/checkpoint files, normal shutdown and process exit.
scope_definitions.metadata_wall_seconds: CPU steady_clock cumulative interval per current seed, from immediately before its first accumulation DispatchRays call through synchronous radiance EXR save at this checkpoint. Earlier checkpoints are included. Timer resets only for a new seed or invalidating scene reset; no reset for64->256->1024. Not GPU-only.
scope_definitions.sum_final_checkpoint: Sum only the largest-SPP checkpoint once per seed. Summing every checkpoint double-counts nested time.
scope_definitions.metadata_excluded: Application/scene/pipeline initialization before first timed dispatch; work after the final checkpoint clock is sampled (metadata write itself, completion/close polling, final frame end/present, render-thread join, queue idle waits, object teardown/process exit); inter-seed work outside timer windows.
scope_definitions.validation_mode: These receipts say pt_validation=false, so validation-AOV exports/readback-ring drain code is compiled out. Boilerplate timing_scope mentions their possible cost but they cannot explain the observed110s here.

findings.claim: Constant scatter Application115.7946544s minus four final seed timers5.39902413s leaves110.39563027s outside those windows. Ramp g-.5 likewise115.4137186s minus5.31651782s leaves110.09720078s.

Constant and ramp g-.5 final metadata were written roughly109.16s and108.79s before final receipt completion. Therefore the dominant delay lies after checkpoint output, not in the already-timed radiance accumulation or ordinary initial scene loading.

A completed automation batch returns before any further PathTracer dispatch. Exit is polled by the game thread; engine release joins the render thread, flushes queues and destroys scene/renderer resources.

Existing stdout has no per-phase timestamps or stack samples. Cannot assign the long post-output delay specifically to the game thread, join, fence wait, resource destruction, driver/PIX teardown, or another exit cost. These are candidate phase locations, not measured attributions.
The wrapper adds about0.4s for these jobs; Python polling/import alone does not explain the roughly110s Application tail. No intentional100s delay appears in the inspected exit/batch code.

report_wording: Record116.19s as whole job/process elapsed, not render-only. The constant-scatter timed accumulation/readback windows sum5.40s across four seeds. A separately observed post-checkpoint shutdown/exit delay is not yet phase-attributed. Stage4 needs separately instrumented, isolated timing before comparing heterogeneous-medium slowdown.
future_stage4_requirements: Separate startup, first dispatch, final radiance save, close signal, render join, each queue flush and object teardown timestamps.
Use actual GPU timestamp around PathTracer dispatch for GPU kernel cost; retain end-to-end time separately.
Compare equal scene/seed/SPP/depth/SPF settings; nested checkpoints are not independent one-shot runs.
Record overlapping CPU/GPU workloads; current campaign timings are observational, not isolated benchmark conclusions.
changes: No production/source edits, new rendering or GPU work; analysis of current source and existing artifacts only.
